result.summary: This pull request raises the minimum C++ language standard to C++23 across CMake, depends, and CI configurations, requiring GCC 13 or Clang 19. It replaces internal polyfills and workarounds—such as util::Expected, ALWAYS_FALSE, and custom byteswap routines—with standard library equivalents including std::expected, static_assert(false), and std::byteswap. It also mechanically refactors string lookups to use string::contains and adopts std::views::zip in the kernel block import loop.
result.problem: Remaining on C++20 forces Bitcoin Core to maintain custom compatibility polyfills and prevents using C++23 standard library utilities, despite downstream components like libmultiprocess already adopting C++23 syntax.
evidence: Author notes in the description that 'the workarounds to avoid C++23 keep accumulating and some parts of the code already use C++23 features, such as lambda attributes (https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/commit/bdd0cd69418d189f62699d274a751cbf6d36bb43).'
Author highlights that switching to C++23 unblocks broader modernization tracked in #34979.
result.scope_notes: Spans 54 files, mostly due to mechanical replacements of string find checks with .contains() via clang-tidy, alongside updates to CMake, depends, and CI build flags.
result.changed_since_previous: Added an IWYU cleanup commit that adds explicit <expected> headers to callers and removes obsolete <util/expected.h> inclusions.
result.card: This pull request bumps the minimum required C++ standard to C++23 across CMake, depends, and CI, setting minimum compiler versions to GCC 13 and Clang 19. It replaces in-tree polyfills like util::Expected and byteswap macros with std::expected and std::byteswap, and adopts C++23 features such as string::contains and std::views::zip across 54 files. The author notes that workarounds to avoid C++23 continue to accumulate while dependencies such as libmultiprocess already rely on C++23 features. This RFC is intended to unblock further modernization tracked in #34979.

risk.why: Raising minimum compiler versions will break build environments for packagers and developers running older distributions without GCC 13 or Clang 19.
